claims.claim_text: 5G Network Deployment: 'We have deployed 5G VoNR covering over 220 million Americans' and offering '5G broadband service to over 268 million Americans.' Per Jan 10, 2025 FCC filing, EchoStar certified 5G broadband service to >=80% of U.S. population by Dec 31, 2024 for AWS-4, 700MHz, H-Block and 600MHz licenses (Commitments #2 and #3 of Extension Request).
claims.rubric: HIGH — quantified physical infrastructure / regulatory build-out milestone testable against FCC filings and against operating-segment KPIs.

claims.claim_text: Wireless spectrum licenses commitment: 'We have invested a total of over $30 billion to acquire certain Wireless spectrum licenses.' Total carrying amount $38.99B (including $9.5B capitalized interest) as of Dec 31, 2024. FCC granted Extension Request that pushes certain final deadlines from June 14, 2025 to Dec 14, 2026 conditional on commitments, including deploying at least 24,000 5G sites by June 14, 2025.
claims.rubric: HIGH — quantified spectrum investment and FCC build-out obligations are public-record testable; absence of FCC build-out enforcement actions or finding-in-favor of EchoStar is meaningful.

claims.claim_text: Total debt, finance lease and other obligations outstanding = $26.603 billion as of Dec 31, 2024.  Long-term debt + interest schedule totals $53.1B over 5 years.  Recent capital actions include $5.356B 10-3/4% Senior Secured Notes due 2029, $1.906B 3-7/8% Convertible Secured Notes due 2030, $2.5B New DISH DBS Financing from TPG Angelo Gordon at 10.75% rising to 11.25%, and $400M PIPE at $28.04/share (Nov 2024).  Related-party $100M backstop from a Charles Ergen-related party on the 10-3/4% notes and DTV terminated DISH DBS sale in Nov 2024.  These are unambiguous distress markers.
claims.rubric: HIGH — material going-concern-adjacent distress markers.  Calibration Heuristic 10 (delisting/going-concern). Distressed financing terms (10.75-11.25% senior secured, 13.25-13.75% preferred, related-party backstop) and DTV walk-away are all forensic flags.
